title: Éliphas Lévi → Golden Dawn → Crowley — Codex Admission Catalog
scope: Tarot/Hebrew correspondence lineage, conflicts, and HNK governance implications

items.name: Éliphas Lévi Tarot ↔ Hebrew-letter scheme
items.description: Lévi's 22-fold alignment of Tarot trumps with the Hebrew alphabet, with the numbered trumps following alphabetical order and the Fool assigned to Shin near the end.
items.admission_reason: Foundational for the later Western occult Tarot/Hebrew lineage and necessary to explain Golden Dawn departures.
items.risk_or_limit: Not evidence for ancient Tarot origins or universal Hebrew-letter correspondences.

sources.title: Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie
sources.author: Éliphas Lévi

items.name: Lévi placement of the Fool at Shin
items.description: In Lévi's scheme the Fool is associated with Shin, between Judgement/Resh and the World/Tav rather than being placed first with Aleph.
items.admission_reason: Useful as a concrete marker distinguishing Lévi's system from the later Golden Dawn system.
items.risk_or_limit: Do not treat this placement as historically original to Tarot or Hebrew tradition.

items.name: Cipher Manuscript reindexing: Fool → Aleph
items.description: The Golden Dawn Cipher Manuscript lineage moves the Fool to Aleph and shifts the following trumps accordingly, forming the familiar modern occult sequence.
items.admission_reason: Explains the transition from Lévi's alignment to the correspondence architecture inherited by the source PDF.
items.risk_or_limit: It is a deliberate later systematization, not a neutral restoration of an ancient Tarot order.

items.name: Golden Dawn Strength ↔ Justice interchange
items.description: The Golden Dawn interchanges Strength and Justice relative to older printed numbering so Teth aligns with Leo and Lamed with Libra.
items.admission_reason: High-value genealogical fingerprint for identifying Golden Dawn-derived correspondence tables.
items.risk_or_limit: The swap is system-specific and should not be flattened into a universal Tarot fact.

items.name: Liber AL I:57 — Tzaddi is not the Star
items.description: Crowley's Liber AL vel Legis contains the explicit statement that Tzaddi is not the Star, creating a conflict with the inherited Golden Dawn attribution.
items.admission_reason: Primary-source trigger for Crowley's later redesign of the Emperor/Star correspondence.
items.risk_or_limit: The verse states a rejection but does not itself specify the replacement mapping; later mapping is Crowley's interpretation.

items.name: Crowley Emperor ↔ Star reassignment
items.description: Crowley resolves Liber AL I:57 by assigning Tzaddi to the Emperor and Heh to the Star, counterchanging the inherited Golden Dawn pair.
items.admission_reason: Essential example of an internal tradition deliberately revising an inherited correspondence system.
items.risk_or_limit: This is a Thelemic redesign, not a Sefer Yetzirah requirement and not universally accepted outside Crowley's system.

items.name: Heh/Tzaddi versioned conflict set
items.description: The Golden Dawn and Crowley/Thoth systems preserve incompatible Heh/Tzaddi Tarot assignments that must coexist as versioned correspondence sets.
items.admission_reason: Directly validates the Codex rule that conflicting traditions must coexist with provenance rather than being silently harmonized.
items.risk_or_limit: Core status applies to the versioning/conflict rule, not to either occult mapping as HNK doctrine.

items.name: Correspondence-set identity by tradition
items.description: A correspondence must carry a tradition/system identity such as LEVI, GOLDEN_DAWN, or THOTH rather than being stored as an unqualified universal mapping.
items.admission_reason: Prevents data corruption when several historically documented mappings disagree.
items.risk_or_limit: Does not adjudicate which tradition is metaphysically true; it preserves traceable claims.

items.name: Card number ≠ Hebrew-letter position
items.description: Tarot card numbering and Hebrew alphabetical position are separate data dimensions and must not be collapsed into a single ordinal.
items.admission_reason: Lévi, Golden Dawn and Crowley demonstrate that the same symbolic entities can be reordered without changing all identifiers.
items.risk_or_limit: Applies as a data-model rule; it does not imply that every alternative ordering is equally historically grounded.

items.name: Symmetry as a symbolic design heuristic
items.description: Crowley explicitly uses zodiacal symmetry as part of his justification for the Emperor/Star reassignment.
items.admission_reason: Potentially useful as a design-validation heuristic when constructing HNK symbolic systems.
items.risk_or_limit: Aesthetic or structural symmetry is not evidence that a metaphysical claim is objectively true.

items.name: Revelatory override does not auto-promote canon
items.description: A claimed revelation may motivate a tradition-specific redesign, but it cannot automatically override documented source mappings inside HNK governance.
items.admission_reason: Protects the Codex from silently converting private or tradition-specific revelation into universal canonical fact.
items.risk_or_limit: Does not deny spiritual meaning; it constrains how claims are represented in the shared Codex.

items.name: Tradition-preserving redesign
items.description: A symbolic system may intentionally redesign inherited correspondences while preserving the older system as a distinct historical layer.
items.admission_reason: Provides a clean model for creating HNK-authored mappings without falsely claiming them as ancient correspondences.
items.risk_or_limit: Every redesigned mapping must declare authorship, rationale, version, dependencies and conflicts.

items.name: Authored-mapping provenance lock
items.description: Any correspondence created specifically for HNK must be marked HNK_AUTHORED and may not inherit historical authority merely because it resembles an older system.
items.admission_reason: Makes original HNK design possible without falsifying genealogy.
items.risk_or_limit: Requires explicit source/author/version metadata on every HNK-authored mapping.

items.name: Crowley phonetic-etymological rationale for Tzaddi/Emperor
items.description: Crowley supplements his reassignment with comparative phonetic/etymological associations linking Tzaddi-like sounds to rulership terms.
items.admission_reason: Useful for understanding Crowley's internal reasoning and the way symbolic systems justify redesigns.
items.risk_or_limit: The etymological argument is not a reliable historical-linguistic derivation and should not be operationalized as fact.

items.name: Lévi → Cipher Manuscript → Golden Dawn → Crowley lineage
items.description: Versioned genealogy showing successive redesign of Tarot/Hebrew correspondences from Lévi through the Cipher Manuscript and Golden Dawn to Crowley's Thoth revision.
items.admission_reason: Provides the traceable lineage necessary to explain why multiple incompatible occult tables exist.
items.risk_or_limit: The chain describes the specific modern Western occult correspondence lineage, not the total history of Kabbalah or Tarot.

items.name: Tarot as interface layer, not mandatory ontology
items.description: The comparative lineage shows Tarot can function as an interface laid over Hebrew-letter/path systems rather than being intrinsic to the older Sefer Yetzirah core.
items.admission_reason: Allows HNK to use Tarot as an optional representational interface without making it a mandatory foundation of the runtime.
items.risk_or_limit: Requires separate decisions for any specific Tarot mapping used operationally.
